hero_title: Best time to visit — or host — in Marrakech.
hero_subtitle: Month by month: weather, prices, Ramadan and the city’s busiest weeks.

sections.html:
Marrakech works most of the year, but the right month depends on what you are planning. A private dinner in Agafay needs a different season from a week of gardens and hammams.

Spring: March to May

The most popular season. Days are warm, evenings are mild enough to dine outside, and the Atlas often still has snow on the peaks. The best houses fill early, so plan four to six months ahead.

Summer: June to August

Midday heat makes long outings hard, but evenings on a rooftop or in the desert are beautiful. Summer suits slower days built around late starts, pools and evening plans — and rates are often lower.

Autumn: September to November

The second peak. Temperatures fall back to comfortable levels and the light is soft — one of the country’s most flattering moments.

Winter: December to February

Sunny days and cold nights. Fireplaces, hammams and heated tents work well, and the year-end holidays are busy.

For a desert dinner, the best months are usually March to May and late September to early November.

Planning around Ramadan

Ramadan moves about eleven days earlier each year. Journeys run normally, with some changes to opening hours and dining. Many guests enjoy an iftar as part of the experience. Check the dates for your year before you fix a plan.

Quick checklist

  • Check Ramadan and public holiday dates for your year
  • Hold the best houses four to six months ahead for spring and autumn
  • Have a covered backup for any outdoor dinner
  • Allow time in the day for the heat in summer
